import re

context = """Bernhard is a frog.
Lily is a frog.
Lily is gray.
Brian is a lion.
Greg is a swan.
Julius is a swan.
Greg is gray.
Brian is white.
Julius is gray."""

colors = {"gray", "white", "red", "green", "blue", "yellow", "black", "brown"}
species_of, color_of = {}, {}
for line in context.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r"(\w+) is (?:a|an) (\w+)\.", line.strip())
    if m:
        species_of[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
        continue
    m = re.match(r"(\w+) is (\w+)\.", line.strip())
    if m and m.group(2) in colors:
        color_of[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)

# Strict entailment: no explicit color or universal rule for Bernhard
print("Explicit color for Bernhard:", color_of.get("Bernhard"))

# Regularity in context: colors per species among known individuals
by_species = {}
for name, sp in species_of.items():
    if name in color_of:
        by_species.setdefault(sp, set()).add(color_of[name])
print("Colors observed per species:", by_species)

uniform = all(len(v) == 1 for v in by_species.values())
print("Every species has a uniform color in the context:", uniform)

sp = species_of["Bernhard"]
inferred = by_species.get(sp)
print("Bernhard's species:", sp, "-> inferred color set:", inferred)

submitted = "The color of Bernhard is not specified in the provided context."
if uniform and inferred and len(inferred) == 1:
    expected = next(iter(inferred))
    print("Expected answer from context regularity:", expected)
    if expected in submitted.lower():
        print("CHECK PASS")
    else:
        print("Submitted answer does not give", expected, "(the only frog with a known color, Lily, is gray)")
        print("CHECK FAIL")
else:
    print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
